explainers.title: A Message Is One Number Between Zero and One
explainers.summary: Step an arithmetic coder forward one symbol at a time and watch a single interval narrow until its width is the probability of the whole message.

explainers.title: Two Auctions, Two Sets of Bids, One Revenue
explainers.summary: Run a first-price and a second-price auction on exactly the same bidders. The bids look nothing alike and the seller earns the same.

sources.title: Vickrey, Counterspeculation, Auctions, and Competitive Sealed Tenders, J. Finance 16(1), 1961
Myerson, Optimal Auction Design, Mathematics of Operations Research 6(1), 1981

explainers.title: Sensitivity Is The Least Important Number
explainers.summary: Tune a test until a positive result actually means something. The number that moves the answer is almost never the one printed on the box.

sources.title: Gigerenzer and Hoffrage, How to Improve Bayesian Reasoning Without Instruction: Frequency Formats (1995)
Casscells, Schoenberger and Graboys, Interpretation by Physicians of Clinical Laboratory Results (1978)
US Preventive Services Task Force, Screening for Breast Cancer: recommendation statement

explainers.title: Tuning by the Wobble
explainers.summary: Two close tones pulse at exactly their frequency difference. Slide the second string until the pulsing stops and you have tuned by ear, without ever knowing either pitch.

sources.title: Piano tuning: setting the temperament by beat rates

explainers.title: The Slower Algorithm Wins For A While
explainers.summary: Race insertion sort against merge sort, move the constant factor merge sort pays, and watch the size where the quadratic algorithm finally loses slide across the range real libraries tune for.

sources.title: Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 3: Sorting and Searching, section 5.2.4
Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, chapters 2 and 4
Tim Peters, listsort.txt: the description of Timsort in the CPython source

explainers.title: Draw Any Population You Like
explainers.summary: Draw a population as lopsided as you can and watch the exact distribution of its sample mean become a bell curve anyway, at a rate you can read off the screen.

sources.title: Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Vol. I, Ch. X
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §1.3.6.6.1 Normal Distribution

explainers.title: The Rule of 72 Is Only Honest at One Rate
explainers.summary: Scrub through sixty years of compound growth, watch the doublings arrive on a fixed clock, and see where the rule of 72 stops telling the truth.

explainers.title: Your Interval Either Contains It Or It Does Not
explainers.summary: Draw a population, then watch a hundred confidence intervals appear and roughly five of them miss. The ninety-five is a property of the recipe, not of the interval in front of you.

sources.title: Neyman, Outline of a Theory of Statistical Estimation Based on the Classical Theory of Probability (1937)
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 1.3.6.7.2: critical values of the t distribution
Morey, Hoekstra, Rouder, Lee and Wagenmakers, The Fallacy of Placing Confidence in Confidence Intervals (2016)

explainers.title: One Number Decides How a Thing Stops Shaking
explainers.summary: Move the damping ratio and find the boundary where a system stops ringing and starts creeping, and why more damping past that point makes things worse.

sources.title: Feynman Lectures on Physics, Vol. I Ch. 24 — Transients
Ogata, Modern Control Engineering — second-order system response

explainers.title: A Guess About Distance Is Worth Half the Search
explainers.summary: Step two shortest-path searches through a maze one expansion at a time and watch a rough distance estimate halve the work without costing a step of path.

sources.title: Hart, Nilsson & Raphael (1968), A Formal Basis for the Heuristic Determination of Minimum Cost Paths
Amit Patel, Introduction to A* — Red Blob Games

explainers.title: Two Terms, One Pattern
explainers.summary: Assemble the double-slit pattern one part at a time and see that the fringe spacing comes from the slit separation while the brightness envelope comes from the slit width.

sources.title: Hecht, Optics — Fraunhofer diffraction by a double slit

explainers.title: A Flat Battery Is Not Empty
explainers.summary: Drag the concentrations in a two-beaker cell and watch its voltage move, then follow the free-energy curve down to the bottom where the voltage is exactly zero.

explainers.title: Which Number Did the Poison Move?
explainers.summary: Add an inhibitor to an enzyme assay and watch which of the two parameters changes — the one that holds still names the mechanism.

sources.title: Enzyme inhibitor — competitive, non-competitive and uncompetitive
Lineweaver–Burk plot and its statistical problems

explainers.title: Herd Immunity Is Not Where It Stops
explainers.summary: Guess how many people an unmitigated epidemic infects, then watch it sail past the herd immunity threshold and keep going.

sources.title: Kermack and McKendrick, A Contribution to the Mathematical Theory of Epidemics, Proc. R. Soc. A 115, 1927
Miller, A Note on the Derivation of Epidemic Final Sizes, Bull. Math. Biol. 74(9), 2012

explainers.title: Every Interval Slightly Wrong, On Purpose
explainers.summary: Put a just interval beside its equal-tempered twin, watch the beats appear, and see where the twelve-tone compromise spends its error.

explainers.title: The Gaps Between Numbers Are Not All the Same Size
explainers.summary: Slide the magnitude up and watch the gap between neighbouring doubles double at every power of two, until whole integers start going missing.

sources.title: Goldberg, What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic, ACM Computing Surveys 23(1), 1991

explainers.title: Building a Corner Out of Curves
explainers.summary: Stack sine waves one at a time into a square wave and watch the overshoot beside the jump narrow without ever getting shorter.

explainers.title: The Gear in the Middle Does Nothing
explainers.summary: Build a gear train one wheel at a time and watch an idler flip the direction without touching the ratio, while two wheels bolted to one shaft change everything.

sources.title: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, chapter on gear trains

explainers.title: Thirty-Three Degrees
explainers.summary: Balance absorbed sunlight against emitted infrared, add one grey absorbing layer, and read off why Earth is thirty-three degrees warmer than a bare rock.

explainers.title: The Error Tells You Where It Is
explainers.summary: Three parity checks over seven bits, arranged so the checks that fail spell out, in binary, the number of the bit that broke. Flip a bit and watch the circles answer.

sources.title: R. W. Hamming, Error Detecting and Error Correcting Codes (1950)

explainers.title: Timbre Is a List of Numbers
explainers.summary: Stack sine waves one harmonic at a time and watch a square, a sawtooth and a triangle assemble themselves out of nothing but amplitudes.

sources.title: Helmholtz, On the Sensations of Tone, 1877 (Ellis translation)

explainers.title: Your Hash Is Half As Wide As You Think
explainers.summary: A 32-bit hash has four billion slots and reaches even odds of a collision at seventy-seven thousand items. The square root halves your bits, and every table size has the same curve.

sources.title: Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 3, section 6.4

explainers.title: Building an Optimal Code, Two Symbols at a Time
explainers.summary: Step through Huffman's greedy construction and see why merging the two rarest symbols yields a code no other prefix code can beat.

sources.title: D. A. Huffman, A Method for the Construction of Minimum-Redundancy Codes, Proc. IRE 40(9), 1952
Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory, Ch. 5 — Data Compression

explainers.title: Where The Ideal Gas Law Quietly Stops Working
explainers.summary: On a log-log chart PV = nRT is a straight line. Squeeze a real gas and it peels away: below the line while attraction wins, above it once the molecules run out of room.

sources.title: CODATA 2018 value of the molar gas constant

explainers.title: Forty-Two Small Decisions
explainers.summary: Step through the edit-distance table one cell at a time and see that every cell is the same three-way choice, then read the alignment back off the finished grid.

explainers.title: Every Flat Map Is Wrong, and You Pick How
explainers.summary: Drag one circle around the globe across five projections and watch it stretch, shear or hold its area, with both principal scale factors read straight off the projection's derivatives.

sources.title: Snyder, Map Projections: A Working Manual, USGS Professional Paper 1395 (1987)
Tissot, Memoire sur la representation des surfaces (1881)
Gauss, Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas (1827), the Theorema Egregium

explainers.title: Order Two Is Babble, Order Four Is Plagiarism
explainers.summary: Paste a training text, slide the memory of a Markov model from one character to eight, and watch its output cross from noise into verbatim quotation with almost nothing in between.

sources.title: Shannon, A Mathematical Theory of Communication (1948), section 3 on n-gram approximations to English
Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, chapter 3: N-gram Language Models
Carlini and others, Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models (2023)

explainers.title: Draw Anything. It Grows by ad − bc.
explainers.summary: Draw a shape, push the four entries of a 2x2 matrix around, and watch every area multiply by the same number — the determinant — going negative when the plane turns over and zero when it collapses.

explainers.title: The Host Knows, and That Is the Whole Trick
explainers.summary: Play the doors, then take away the host's knowledge and watch the two-thirds advantage vanish, which is where the puzzle's real lesson lives.

sources.title: Selvin, A Problem in Probability, The American Statistician 29(1), 1975
Rosenhouse, The Monty Hall Problem, Oxford University Press, 2009

explainers.title: Where You Start Decides Where You Land
explainers.summary: Newton's method doubles its correct digits every step near a root. Pan the complex plane and watch the map of where each start ends up turn fractal.

sources.title: Cayley, A. (1879), The Newton–Fourier imaginary problem

explainers.title: Why Simpson's Rule Beats the Trapezoid
explainers.summary: Race the trapezoid rule against Simpson's rule and see why one error falls four times faster per halving, for the same function evaluations.

sources.title: Numerical Recipes, 3rd ed., §4.1 Classical Formulas for Equally Spaced Abscissas
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §3.5 Quadrature

explainers.title: Speed Up And You Will Go Slower
explainers.summary: A prograde burn raises the far side of your orbit, never the side you are on, and leaves you slower than you started. Aim the thrust by hand and watch the transfer ellipse miss.

explainers.title: The Flat Part of the Curve
explainers.summary: Titrate a weak acid and watch pH refuse to move, then give way all at once, and find the closed form for how much punishment a buffer absorbs.

explainers.title: Three Knobs, Three Different Ways to Be Wrong
explainers.summary: Tune a PID controller by hand against a target step response and find out what each of the three terms fixes, and what each one breaks.

explainers.title: The Ocean Floor Is a Tape Recorder
explainers.summary: Click anywhere on a synthetic ocean floor to read its age, and recover the spreading rate from the width of the magnetic stripes the way it was first done.

explainers.title: One Number Decides Whether a Population Settles
explainers.summary: Raise the growth rate of a one-line population model and watch it settle, split, split again, and then stop repeating altogether.

sources.title: May, R. M. (1976), Simple mathematical models with very complicated dynamics

explainers.title: Kill Both Sides, Help the Pest
explainers.summary: Explore the Lotka-Volterra phase plane, find that every orbit averages to the equilibrium it never sits at, and see why culling predator and prey together makes the prey more common.

explainers.title: Write a Strategy, Enter the Tournament
explainers.summary: Write your own iterated prisoners dilemma strategy in the page and watch it play a round robin, then turn on noise and see which strategies can recover from a mistake.

explainers.title: The 45-Degree Rule Is a Vacuum Rule
explainers.summary: Fire the same shot into a vacuum and into air, side by side, and watch the parabola lose its symmetry and its best angle drop below 45 degrees.

explainers.title: Sorted Input Is Quicksort's Worst Case
explainers.summary: Race a last-element, random and median-of-three pivot on the same list and watch the textbook version go quadratic on data that is merely already sorted.

explainers.title: The Clock Does Not Care How Much You Started With
explainers.summary: Scrub through geological time and watch the parent-to-daughter ratio give the same age whatever the sample size, then see the isochron rescue the date when the daughter was there from the start.

sources.title: Nicolaysen, Graphic Interpretation of Discordant Age Measurements on Metamorphic Rocks, Ann. NY Acad. Sci. 91, 1961

explainers.title: The Balanced Equation Will Not Tell You This
explainers.summary: Four unlabelled vials of decaying reactant. Tune an order and a rate constant until your law lies on the measurements, and learn to read the order off the shape of the curve.

explainers.title: The Pattern Is Fine. The Engine Is Not.
explainers.summary: Write a regular expression and watch a backtracking engine take exponential time on an input that a finite automaton finishes in a straight line.

sources.title: Russ Cox — Regular Expression Matching Can Be Simple And Fast
OWASP — Regular expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)

explainers.title: Nobody Did Anything and It Improved
explainers.summary: Pick the top scorers and test them again. They fall back with no cause at all, and that alone is enough to manufacture a treatment effect that never happened.

sources.title: Galton, Regression Towards Mediocrity in Hereditary Stature (1886)
Barnett, van der Pols and Dobson, Regression to the mean: what it is and how to deal with it

explainers.title: Three Against Four Takes Twelve Beats
explainers.summary: Two rhythms of different lengths drift apart and snap back only at their least common multiple. Scrub through the cycle and watch the downbeats miss each other for eleven beats.

sources.title: Toussaint, The Euclidean Algorithm Generates Traditional Musical Rhythms

explainers.title: Nobody Wanted This
explainers.summary: Paint a mixed neighbourhood, give every square a mild preference for similar neighbours, and watch it separate anyway — the pattern does not reveal the preference.

sources.title: Thomas C. Schelling — Dynamic Models of Segregation (1971)

explainers.title: The Line You Cannot Cross
explainers.summary: Guess whether a noisy channel can carry your message reliably at a chosen rate, then see the hard boundary that no code of any block length can get past.

explainers.title: Every Group One Way, Everyone the Other
explainers.summary: Build a table where one group is admitted at a higher rate in every programme and a lower rate overall, then split the pooled gap exactly into a treatment part and a placement part.

sources.title: Bickel, Hammel & O'Connell, Sex Bias in Graduate Admissions: Data from Berkeley, Science 187 (1975) 398-404
Charig, Webb, Payne & Wickham, Comparison of treatment of renal calculi, BMJ 292 (1986) 879-882
Simpson, The Interpretation of Interaction in Contingency Tables, JRSS B 13 (1951) 238-241
Blyth, On Simpson's Paradox and the Sure-Thing Principle, JASA 67 (1972) 364-366

explainers.title: Seven Vowels Move and None Collide
explainers.summary: Step through the Great Vowel Shift one change at a time and watch seven long vowels cross the mouth over two centuries without any two of them ever landing on the same spot.

sources.title: Chain shift: push chains and pull chains

explainers.title: The Longer Way Round
explainers.summary: Put a light clock at rest beside the same clock in motion, drag the photon along both paths, and read the Lorentz factor straight off the triangle.

explainers.title: The Law Says Who Pays, the Market Decides Who Bears It
explainers.summary: Drag two elasticities and watch a tax burden slide between buyers and sellers, while the side the law taxes makes no difference at all.

explainers.title: Everyone Is Right and the Field Is Ruined
explainers.summary: Every herder's own best move is one more animal, and the common ends up carrying nearly twice what it should. Drag the number of herders and watch the gap open.

sources.title: Cournot competition, the same first-order condition
